name: Regional anatomy
description: Anatomy by region of the body, as it is met in clinical practice: the head and neck, the trunk (back, thorax, abdomen and pelvis) and the limbs. Landmarks, spaces and triangles, what runs where, and the common injuries that follow from it. Revision of the other chapters is a good start.

source.name: Written for Study Buddy. Pictures rendered from BodyParts3D (© The Database Center for Life Science, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP).

questions.prompt: Which muscle divides each side of the neck into an anterior and a posterior triangle?
questions.explanation: The posterior triangle lies between sternocleidomastoid and trapezius, with the clavicle as its base.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which nerve, often hurt in operations in the posterior triangle of the neck, supplies trapezius?
questions.explanation: It runs superficially, and is easily cut. Injury gives a drooping shoulder.

questions.prompt: What are the contents of the carotid sheath in the neck?
answers: Common carotid artery, internal jugular vein and vagus nerve
Carotid artery, jugular vein, vagus nerve
wrong: Phrenic nerve, vagus nerve and subclavian artery
External carotid artery, facial vein and hypoglossal nerve
questions.explanation: The artery is medial, the vein lateral and the nerve between them and behind.

questions.prompt: Where can the carotid pulse be felt?
answers: In the neck, in front of the sternocleidomastoid, beside the larynx
At the front of the neck, beside the larynx
wrong: Behind the angle of the jaw only
At the back of the neck
questions.explanation: At about the level of the upper border of the thyroid cartilage, where the common carotid divides.

questions.prompt: At which vertebral level is the cricoid cartilage, the lower end of the larynx?
questions.explanation: A landmark for starting the trachea and the oesophagus.

questions.prompt: At which vertebral level is the hyoid bone?
questions.explanation: It lies at the level of the mandible's angle. It is the only bone that does not meet another bone.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How many cranial fossae are there on the inside of the base of the skull, and what are they called?
wrong: Four: frontal, temporal, parietal and occipital
questions.explanation: The frontal lobes sit in the anterior fossa, the temporal lobes in the middle and the cerebellum in the posterior.

questions.prompt: Which opening in the occipital bone lets the spinal cord join the brainstem?

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which perforated plate of the ethmoid bone lets the olfactory nerve fibres through?
questions.explanation: A fracture here can leak cerebrospinal fluid from the nose.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which opening in the sphenoid bone lets the optic nerve into the orbit?
questions.explanation: The ophthalmic artery goes with it.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which nerves go through the superior orbital fissure to the eye muscles?
answers: The oculomotor, trochlear and abducens (III, IV and VI)
questions.explanation: Along with the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve.

questions.prompt: Which weak spot on the side of the skull, where four bones meet, covers the middle meningeal artery?
questions.explanation: A blow to it can tear the artery, causing an extradural haematoma.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which suture joins the frontal bone to the two parietal bones?
questions.explanation: The sagittal suture joins the two parietals; the lambdoid joins them to the occipital.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Why can a newborn's skull change shape during birth?
answers: The bones are not yet joined, with gaps (fontanelles) between them
The skull has fontanelles and open sutures
wrong: The skull bones are cartilage only
The skull is made of one bone
questions.explanation: The anterior fontanelle closes at about 18 months.

questions.prompt: Which paranasal sinus is in the cheek, and is the largest?
questions.explanation: Its opening is high on the wall, so it drains poorly when upright.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which joint between the mandible and the temporal bone allows chewing?
questions.explanation: It is a hinge and gliding joint, with a disc.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which four muscles are the muscles of mastication?
answers: Masseter, temporalis, medial and lateral pterygoids
Masseter, temporalis and the two pterygoids
wrong: Buccinator, orbicularis oris, platysma and mentalis
questions.explanation: All are supplied by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve.

questions.prompt: Which cranial nerve supplies the muscles of facial expression?
questions.explanation: Damage, as in Bell's palsy, causes a one-sided droop of the face.

questions.prompt: Which large salivary gland sits in front of the ear, and is crossed by branches of the facial nerve?
questions.explanation: The duct opens opposite the upper second molar.

questions.prompt: What are the three divisions of the trigeminal nerve?
questions.explanation: They supply the skin of the forehead, the cheek and the jaw.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest cartilage of the larynx, forming the Adam's apple?
questions.explanation: More prominent in men.

questions.prompt: Which vertebra has a long spinous process that can be felt at the base of the neck?
questions.explanation: A landmark for counting the vertebrae.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which are the primary curves of the spine, present at birth, curving backwards (kyphosis)?
questions.explanation: The cervical and lumbar curves, which curve forwards (lordosis), develop after birth.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: At about which vertebral level does the adult spinal cord end?
questions.explanation: It ends at the conus medullaris. Below that, the nerve roots form the cauda equina, so a lumbar puncture is done at L3 to L4.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Between which vertebrae is a lumbar puncture usually done?
answers: L3 and L4 (or L4 and L5)
questions.explanation: The iliac crests, at L4, are the guide.

questions.prompt: What are the five fused vertebrae at the back of the pelvis called?
questions.explanation: The coccyx is the tail below.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Where is the sternal angle, and which landmark does it mark?
answers: Between the manubrium and the body of the sternum, where the second rib joins
wrong: At the xiphoid process, where the seventh rib joins
At the clavicle, at the level of the first rib
At the navel, at the level of L3
questions.explanation: It marks the level of T4 to T5, where the trachea divides and the aortic arch begins and ends.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: At which vertebral level is the jugular (suprasternal) notch?
At which vertebral level is the xiphisternal joint?
questions.explanation: It lies at about the level of the top of the liver and the heart's lower border.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: In which position do the intercostal vessels and nerve run along each rib?
answers: In the groove under the rib's lower border (vein, artery, nerve from above down)
Along the lower border of the rib
wrong: Along the upper border of the rib
Through the middle of the muscle
On the surface of the rib
questions.explanation: So a chest drain is put in over the top of the rib below. 'VAN' from above down.

questions.prompt: How many true ribs, false ribs and floating ribs are there on each side?
questions.explanation: True ribs join the sternum directly. False ribs join it through the costal cartilage above. The last two are free.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: At which vertebral levels do the vena cava, the oesophagus and the aorta pass through the diaphragm?
questions.explanation: 'I ate ten eggs at twelve': IVC at 8, oesophagus at 10, aortic hiatus at 12.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which of the following lies in the superior mediastinum?
questions.explanation: The heart is in the middle mediastinum, inside the pericardium.

questions.prompt: Where does most lymph from the breast drain?
questions.explanation: About 75%. Some goes to the parasternal nodes.

questions.prompt: Which three flat muscles form the lateral abdominal wall, from outside in?
answers: External oblique, internal oblique, transversus abdominis
External oblique, internal oblique and transversus
wrong: Rectus abdominis, external oblique, internal oblique
questions.explanation: Their fibres run in different directions, like plywood.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the tendinous midline of the front of the abdominal wall, between the two rectus muscles, called?
questions.explanation: A hernia may come through it above the navel.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What passes through the inguinal canal in men?
questions.explanation: In women it carries the round ligament of the uterus.

questions.prompt: Which hernia passes through the deep inguinal ring, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels?
questions.explanation: The commonest hernia, often in the young. A direct hernia goes through the weak back wall of the canal.

questions.prompt: Where is McBurney's point, a landmark for the appendix?
answers: Two thirds of the way from the navel to the right anterior superior iliac spine
A third of the way from the right iliac spine to the navel
wrong: At the midpoint of the left costal margin
questions.explanation: Tenderness there suggests appendicitis.

questions.prompt: At which vertebral level is the transpyloric plane, midway between the jugular notch and the pubic symphysis?
questions.explanation: It passes through the pylorus, the pancreas's neck, the kidneys' hila and the gallbladder fundus.

questions.prompt: At which vertebral level does the coeliac trunk leave the aorta?
questions.explanation: The superior mesenteric artery leaves at L1, the renal arteries at L1 to L2 and the inferior mesenteric at L3.

questions.prompt: At which vertebral level does the aorta divide into the common iliac arteries?
questions.explanation: At about the level of the iliac crests and the navel.

questions.prompt: What is the double fold of peritoneum that attaches the small bowel to the back wall of the abdomen called?
questions.explanation: It carries the blood vessels and nerves.

questions.prompt: What is the apron-like fold of peritoneum hanging from the stomach over the bowel called?
questions.explanation: The 'policeman of the abdomen', as it walls off areas of infection.

questions.prompt: What divides the greater (false) pelvis from the lesser (true) pelvis?
questions.explanation: The lesser pelvis holds the bladder, rectum and reproductive organs.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the diamond-shaped region between the pubic symphysis, the ischial tuberosities and the coccyx called?
questions.explanation: Divided into an anterior urogenital and a posterior anal triangle.

questions.prompt: Which muscle group forms the main part of the pelvic floor?
questions.explanation: It supports the pelvic organs and helps with continence.

figure.alt: The pelvic floor muscles, in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How does the female pelvis differ from the male?
answers: It is wider and shallower, with a larger, rounder inlet and a wider pubic arch
Wider, with a wider subpubic angle
wrong: It is narrower and deeper, with a heart-shaped inlet
It has a smaller pubic arch
questions.explanation: Adapted for childbirth.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the main contents of the axilla?
answers: Axillary artery and vein, brachial plexus and lymph nodes
Axillary vessels, the brachial plexus, lymph nodes
wrong: Subclavian artery, phrenic nerve and thymus
Brachial artery, radial nerve and fat only
Cephalic vein and the intercostal nerves only
questions.explanation: Fat fills the spaces.

questions.prompt: Which spinal nerve roots form the brachial plexus?
answers: C5, C6, C7, C8 and T1
questions.explanation: Roots, trunks, divisions, cords and branches: 'Real Texans Drink Cold Beer'.

questions.prompt: Which nerve winds around the surgical neck of the humerus, and is at risk in a fracture there?
questions.explanation: It supplies deltoid. Damage causes a flat shoulder and loss of skin sensation over it.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which nerve runs in the radial groove at the back of the humerus, at risk in a fracture of the shaft?
questions.explanation: Damage causes wrist drop.

questions.prompt: Which nerve passes behind the medial epicondyle of the humerus (the 'funny bone')?
questions.explanation: Damage gives a claw hand.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which nerve is squeezed in carpal tunnel syndrome?
questions.explanation: It causes tingling in the thumb, index and middle fingers, and weak thumb movement.

questions.prompt: What forms the roof of the carpal tunnel?
questions.explanation: The floor is the carpal bones. The tunnel holds the median nerve and nine flexor tendons.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the contents of the cubital fossa, from lateral to medial?
answers: Biceps tendon, brachial artery and median nerve
Biceps tendon, brachial artery, median nerve
wrong: Radial nerve, ulnar nerve and basilic vein
Median nerve, ulnar nerve and radial artery
Cephalic vein, biceps tendon and ulnar nerve
questions.explanation: The median cubital vein runs on top: the usual place to take blood.

questions.prompt: Which small hollow at the base of the thumb, tender in a scaphoid fracture, is bounded by tendons of the thumb extensors?
questions.explanation: The scaphoid's blood supply is poor, so a fracture heals slowly.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which four muscles form the rotator cuff?
answers: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis
SITS: supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor, subscapularis
wrong: Supraspinatus, teres major, latissimus dorsi and pectoralis major
Trapezius, rhomboids, serratus anterior and levator scapulae
questions.explanation: They hold the head of the humerus in the shallow glenoid cavity.

figure.alt: The rotator cuff muscles, in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Where is the clavicle most often broken?
answers: At the junction of its middle and outer thirds
questions.explanation: The weakest point, where its two curves meet.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the contents of the femoral triangle, from lateral to medial?
answers: Femoral nerve, artery and vein (NAV), and the deep inguinal nodes
wrong: Sciatic nerve, femoral artery and vein
questions.explanation: The femoral pulse is felt just below the midpoint of the inguinal ligament.

figure.alt: The sartorius muscle, in red, which forms its lateral border
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: In which order do the femoral vein, artery and nerve lie in the femoral triangle, from medial to lateral?
questions.explanation: From lateral to medial it spells NAV, or NAVEL with the empty space and the lymphatics: Nerve, Artery, Vein, Empty space, Lymphatics.

questions.prompt: Where is the sciatic nerve in the buttock, and where is it safest to give an injection?
answers: Deep to gluteus maximus; inject in the upper outer quadrant
Inject in the upper outer quadrant
wrong: Inject in the lower inner quadrant
Inject at the centre of the buttock
It lies on the surface of the buttock
questions.explanation: The sciatic nerve runs through the lower, inner quadrant, down the back of the thigh.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part of the femur is the most common site of a hip fracture in older people?
questions.explanation: Its blood supply is easily cut.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which nerve supplies the muscles of the anterior compartment of the thigh (quadriceps)?
questions.explanation: The knee jerk tests it, L2 to L4.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which nerve supplies the hamstring muscles in the posterior compartment of the thigh?
answers: The tibial part of the sciatic nerve

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which nerve supplies the medial (adductor) compartment of the thigh?

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which artery lies deepest in the popliteal fossa, next to the femur?
questions.explanation: From superficial to deep: tibial nerve, popliteal vein, popliteal artery. A popliteal aneurysm is the commonest peripheral aneurysm.

questions.prompt: Which nerve winds around the neck of the fibula, and is at risk in a fracture or tight plaster there?
questions.explanation: Damage causes foot drop.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: How many fascial compartments does the lower leg have?
answers: Four: anterior, lateral, superficial posterior and deep posterior
questions.explanation: Compartment syndrome, from swelling in a tight compartment, is an emergency.

questions.prompt: Which is the strongest and thickest tendon in the body, attached to the heel?
questions.explanation: Joined by gastrocnemius and soleus.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Where can the dorsalis pedis pulse be felt?
answers: On the top of the foot, lateral to the tendon of extensor hallucis longus
On the dorsum of the foot
questions.explanation: The posterior tibial pulse is behind the medial malleolus.

questions.prompt: Which ankle ligaments are most often sprained?
wrong: The collateral ligaments of the knee
questions.explanation: In an inversion injury.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which ligament prevents the tibia from sliding forwards on the femur?
questions.explanation: It is torn in twisting injuries, as in football and skiing.

figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which structures are damaged in the 'unhappy triad' knee injury?
answers: The anterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and medial meniscus
wrong: The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral collateral ligament and lateral meniscus
The patellar ligament, quadriceps tendon and ACL
The ACL, PCL and both collateral ligaments
questions.explanation: From a blow to the outside of the knee.

tests.why: Type each answer from memory, starting with the ones due for review. Small typos are forgiven.
